surface_mechanism_description: Adsorption of Al(CH3)3 or H2O on surface sites followed by reaction to form CH4 and new surface sites S8. The transition state complex TS drives the reaction, and the presence of S8 sites affects further adsorption by altering surface energetics.
evidence: First, one of the two precursors, either Al(CH3)3 or H2O, in the gas phase, A(g), adsorbs on a surface site, S, to yield an adsorbed species, A(ad). A(ad) reacts via a transition state complex, denoted TS, to form CH4 gas and a new surface site, S8. The presence of S8 sites makes further adsorption on remaining S sites energetically less favorable than when precursor is first introduced over a pristine surface having only S sites.
